description: [ECCV 2026 Best Paper Award Candidate] LingBot-Map: Geometric Context Transformer for Streaming 3D Reconstruction

summary.one_liner: LingBot-Map is a feed-forward Geometric Context Transformer model for streaming 3D reconstruction from video or image sequences, with an interactive viser viewer and an offline point-cloud flythrough renderer.
summary.what_it_does: The repository provides the LingBot-Map model code and checkpoints for streaming 3D reconstruction, which estimates camera poses and dense geometry frame by frame. The README describes a Geometric Context Transformer using anchor context, a pose-reference window, and trajectory memory, with a paged KV cache attention design. demo.py runs inference on an image folder or video and opens an interactive browser-based viser viewer, with options for sky masking, keyframe intervals, windowed inference for long sequences, and visualization settings. demo_render/batch_demo.py is an offline pipeline that runs inference and renders a headless point-cloud flythrough MP4, configurable through YAML camera presets. The README also lists an evaluation benchmark for KITTI and Oxford Spires, with preprocessing for Oxford Spires, and says it covers several other datasets in its TODO list.
use_cases: camera pose estimation from image sequences
outdoor drive scene point cloud rendering
benchmarking reconstruction on KITTI or Oxford Spires
how_to_run: conda create -n lingbot-map python=3.10 -y && conda activate lingbot-map
pip install torch==2.8.0 torchvision==0.23.0 --index-url <PyTorch CUDA 12.8 index>
notable: Streaming feed-forward design with paged KV cache, reported at about 20 FPS on 518x378 over sequences over 10,000 frames
Windowed inference and keyframe-interval options for very long sequences
Offline batch renderer that produces point-cloud flythrough MP4s driven by YAML camera paths
Sky masking via an ONNX sky segmentation model, auto-downloaded on first use
Evaluation scripts for KITTI and Oxford Spires
caveats: Performance degrades beyond about 320 views in the KV cache, so long sequences need keyframe or windowed modes; the README notes a maximum inference range bounded by training distances without state resetting
Batch rendering requires NVIDIA Kaolin, which has prebuilt wheels only for specific PyTorch versions (2.8.0 recommended), and CUDA extensions must be built before first run
Some demo datasets and checkpoints are hosted on Hugging Face and ModelScope, and a stronger long-sequence model is marked as coming soon
